newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Oct 31.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Japan may reconsider future grants and technical cooperation to Bangladesh if the government does not resolve "some impediments" in the way of speedy implementation of Japanese-aided projects.
The Asian Development Bank has offered assistence to Bangladesh for facilitating commercial arrangements between Bangladesh and India for the development of a 132 KV double circuit transmission line.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said she would sit with Indian Premier Deve Gowda to resolve the long-standing Ganges water sharing issue by December this year.

The opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has termed the country's present foreign policy as "subservient." The main purpose of the government's foreign policy was to appease India in order to cling to power, BNP said.
Bangladesh and British entrepreneurs on Wednesday explored areas for collaboration in trade and investment.
Police arrested eight persons including seven students from Reshambagan area in Chittagong on charges of possessing illegal firearms.

Finance Minister S A M S Kibria has assessed the latest economic situation with a strong positive note, terming fears expressed by some quarters about "recessionary trends" as not based on "sufficient information."
A British expert on Wednesday said that fashion business needed a proactive rather than reactive approach for successful marketing.
